correctness.rationale: Proof reconstructed: the Weyl projector superoperator is diagonal with eigenvalue D times squared window ambiguity; for normalized N^{-1/2} graph indicator D=N² gives exactly unnormalized translated-intersection Fourier magnitude squared. The congruence 2At=B+A² and valuation of A yield p^j intersections; exact odd-prime-power quadratic Gauss sums give levels p^{2j} and p^{k+l}. Independent enumeration proves the counts L_j and Q_s, with collisions summed. Correctness crosschecked by packaged four-dimensional FFT at (3,1),(5,1),(3,2),(5,2),(3,3), independently enumerated intersection Fourier magnitudes at (3,2),(5,2), and exact integer trace/rank relations. The finite checks are corroboration, not infinite proof; the algebraic proof handles all odd primes, k>=2.

value.rationale: This is a complete natural infinite-family classification of squared singular values of a full finite Gabor intensity sampling operator for a canonical curved sparse window over nonreduced cyclic rings. Exact power-of-p gaps, every multiplicity and zero mode, sharp condition number on the informative operator subspace and the nontrivial asymptotic identifiable fraction p²/(p²+p+1) quantify a genuine p-adic stability/information phenomenon. These precise invariants are useful for lifting-based sampling design and cannot be read off from standard phase-retrieval existence or quadratic-Gauss identities alone. No general nonlinear phase-retrieval claim is made.
